surface_mechanism_description: The two-step growth process at different temperatures allows for the elimination of the trade-off between crystallinity and orientation preference. The first step forms a thin seed layer at 150 °C to control the preferential orientation, and the second step grows the SnS2 at 240 °C to achieve better crystallinity. The (001) basal plane of SnS2 is aligned parallel to the substrate, and the surface morphology changes with temperature, indicating the formation of different crystallographic orientations.
